summary: Midnight dedicated capacity thinness: transient GPU attach failure and noisy-tenant short-stream storm impacting customer p99 and 5xxs
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Acorn Health reported intermittent 5xxs and p99 latency spikes hitting their dedicated pool during the midnight maintenance window on 2026-03-12. Symptoms were concentrated between 00:10-00:25 PDT in us-west-2 and manifested as failed alloc/attach attempts, sudden drop in batch formation, and elevated nvme write latency on the host nodes.

Impact:
- Affected ~12 reserved slots in the customer's dedicated pool; transient throughput degradation led to ~25% of requests returning 5xx or timing out for ~12 minutes.
- Users observed chat completions stalling (stream disconnects) and downstream orchestration retried causing temporary p99 token latency to double.

Timeline (local times):
- 00:08 PDT: customer reports increase in 5xxs via support web UI.
- 00:12-00:18 PDT: telemetry shows nvme.write_latency_ms spike, attach_success_rate drop, and autoscaler interpreted stalled attach metrics as capacity shortage.
- 00:18 PDT: SRE applied temporary customer-level throttle on a noisy tenant identified in pool.
- 00:24 PDT: autoscaler smoothing window adjusted, prefetched snapshots deprioritized; attach rates recovered by 00:26 PDT.

Environment:
- prod-us-west (us-west-2), dedicated pool: pool-acorn-001
- affected models: redwood-neo-7b (default route), llama-2-13b-chat fallback route

Steps to reproduce (suggested):
1) On a staging cluster with a dedicated pool, schedule concurrent background NVMe snapshot writes timed to overlap with a small-stream burst workload.
2) Flood a single tenant with many short, high-qps small-stream requests (50-100ms infer duration) to emulate noisy-tenant behavior.
3) Observe allocator.attach_count, gpu.attach_success, autoscaler.pending_leases, and nvme.write_latency_ms for attach failures and autoscaler misclassification.

Observed behavior:
- Short-lived increase in NVMe write latency coincident with a noisy tenant issuing many sub-200ms streams.
- Allocator attach success rate dropped from ~98% to ~64% for ~8 minutes.
- Autoscaler detected reduced successful attaches and started to shrink predictive capacity, causing further attach stalls and compounding the drop in throughput.
- Streaming connections dropped mid-response; client saw function call timeouts and 5xx.

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler should not shrink capacity during transient IO spikes; allocator should surface NVMe IO errors differently so autoscaler ignores temporary storage pressure.

Logs & metrics references:
- allocator.attach_success_rate (dashboards/allocator/pool-acorn-001)
- nvme.write_latency_ms host graphs (dashboards/hw/io-usw2-aggregates)
- autoscaler.event_log and predictive_capacity_time_series (dashboards/autoscaler/pool-acorn-001)
- support ticket timestamped logs uploaded by customer: s3://support-uploads/acorn/2026-03-12-midnight-logs.tar.gz

Suggested mitigation steps noted up front in ticket: temporary throttle noisy tenant, add snapshotter IO backoff, increase autoscaler smoothing window and minimum capacity during maintenance windows.

investigation_notes: Correlation observed between host nvme.write_latency spikes and allocator.attach_failure_count in pool-acorn-001.

Host-level snapshotter (background checkpoint agent) was performing concurrent checkpoint writes during midnight maintenance window; these writes coincided with a noisy tenant issuing many small streams that stressed NVMe scheduling.
Autoscaler used attach_success_rate as a primary input to reduce predicted capacity; it did not account for short-term storage I/O pressure, causing an avoidable shrink cycle.

Heap of small streams caused many ephemeral CUDA context attaches and small DMA windows; combined with NVMe stalls this increased per-attach latency and transiently exceeded attach timeout thresholds.
Replayed similar workload in staging and reproduced attach fail pattern when we intentionally injected NVMe write latency via fio during short-stream flood.
Telemetry gap: allocator attach latency histogram buckets were coarse; improving granularity would help distinguish IO-induced attach slowdowns from real capacity pressure.
Related prior tickets: SUP-271400 (connection-leak keeping gpu slots reserved) — referenced for allocator heuristics; INT-330 contains autoscaler smoothing config history.
resolution_notes:
Workaround applied (2026-03-12): temporarily throttled identified noisy tenant, adjusted autoscaler smoothing from 2m to 6m for pool-acorn-001, and deprioritized snapshotter IO backoff on affected hosts. Customer confirmed recovery at 00:27 PDT.

Planned permanent actions:
- Deploy autoscaler change that introduces a storage-pressure signal that prevents capacity shrink during NVMe latency events (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/1298).
- Add maintenance-window flag for dedicated pools so autoscaler uses conservative minima during scheduled maintenance.
- Improve attach latency histogram resolution and add a distinct metric allocator.attach_io_latency to separate IO-induced delays.
- Implement snapshotter IO jittering/backoff to avoid synchronized writes across nodes.

Follow-ups created: INT-8891 (platform: storage-pressure signal for autoscaler), INT-8892 (ops: schedule snapshotter smoothing and host jitter), and a customer-facing post-incident note to be sent by CS.

Ticket closed after verification on 2026-03-13 and customer sign-off on 2026-03-13 15:24 PDT.
additional_next_steps: Merge autoscaler PR #1298 and rollout to prod us-west in a canary pool week-of 2026-03-20.
Convene short postmortem with SRE/serving/ops to finalize maintenance-window guidance and publish runbook updates.
Create monitoring alert to detect NVMe write latency coincident with attach_success_rate drops and suppress autoscaler shrink actions when both signals present.
